Horne1, Leeberk Raja Inbaraj2, Jerry S. Zifodya3, Adrienne E. Shapiro4, Adhin Bhaskar2, E. Chandler Church5, Jefferson Daniel6, Alexander W. Kay7, Jonah Kreniske8, Vittoria Lutje9,

sections.title: Page 7

summary.text: Gives background for the LC-aNAAT review, citing 2022 global estimates of TB incidence and rifampicin-resistant TB and WHO's recommendation of rapid molecular tests as initial diagnostics. It explains WHO's grouping of tests into classes and the clinical importance of detecting rifampicin and isoniazid resistance.

sections.extract: Background There were an estimated 10.6 million people who newly developed tuberculosis (TB) in 2022 and of the 7.5 million reported cases, 83% involved the lungs (WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2023). In 2022, there were about 410,000 new cases of rifampicin-resistant or multidrug resistant TB. Several rapid molecular tests are recommended by the WHO as the initial diagnostic test for TB, some of which can detect

summary.text: Describes the STANDARD M10 molecular system and its TB assays, then outlines the review's methods, including literature searches carried out in October 2023 across several databases.

sections.extract: The STANDARD M10 is an in vitro molecular diagnostics system that automatically extracts and amplifies nucleic acids (DNA, RNA) from the collected samples, and analyses the data from amplification in real-time, by combining the processes of isothermal amplification and real-time PCR in a single platform using all-in-one cartridge systems. There are two variations currently available for TB detection: STANDARD™ M10

summary.text: Defines the culture and composite reference standards, then describes data extraction, quality assessment with QUADAS-2 and planned meta-analyses of sensitivity and specificity by subgroup such as smear and HIV status.

sections.extract: Culture (microbiological reference standard) Culture is considered the best reference standard for TB using either automated liquid culture or solid culture methods. Since both culture methods are used interchangeably in clinical practice (Moreira 2015), a positive result either alone or in combination was accepted as a diagnosis of TB while all negative cultures indicated no TB. sections.extract: 507 Background Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) bacteria. TB causes tremendous suffering worldwide and has surpassed HIV/AIDS as the world’s leading infectious cause of death. The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that in 2017, 10 million people became ill with TB globally. Approximately, 1.3 million HIV-negative people and 300,000 HIV-positive people died from TB (WHO 2018).

summary.text: Sets out the background to a WHO-commissioned review of targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) for detecting drug resistance in tuberculosis, explaining that empirical treatment risks failure and amplified resistance where resistance is common. sections.extract: Background Rapid, accurate detection of drug resistance for patients with tuberculosis is an important component within the process of ensuring optimal treatment outcomes both at an individual patient and population level. sections.extract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality globally. Our review aims to summarize the current economic evidence around using targeted Next Generation Sequencing (tNGS) for the diagnosis of DR-TB. Methods: We conducted a systematic review on the economic evaluation of using either tNGS or WGS to diagnose DR-TB. The following three databases were used: PubMed, EMBASE and

sections.title: Page 773

It notes that resistance is concentrated in some high-burden countries and regions. It then explains that conventional phenotypic testing is slow and needs high-level biosafety laboratories and skilled staff.

Novel molecular testing tools are being developed to rapidly detect multi-drug resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) which is needed for more effective and timely treatment of MDR-TB. sections.extract: Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global public health threat. One of the most challenging forms of the disease is multidrug resistant TB (MDR-TB), due to higher morbidity and mortality, complexity of treatment and higher cost (1). WHO estimated that in 2016, close to half a million people were diagnosed with MDR-TB (2). It is estimated that only two out of every three patients with MDR-TB are diagnosed,

sections.extract: Methods Study design This was a cross-sectional observational qualitative study using semi-structured interviews. Setting The main stakeholders were implementers of the FIND trial in the main reference laboratories that implemented the tNGS trial, located in Georgia, India, and South Africa. summary.text: The executive summary of the safety review explains that the tuberculin skin test is known to be safe but that newer antigen-based skin tests had not been systematically assessed. It notes that some studies were at high risk of bias owing to lack of blinding or passive collection of adverse events.

sections.extract: 57 Executive summary Background The diagnostic tests in current use for identification of TB infection are the tuberculin skin test (TST) and interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA). The safety of TST, an in-vivo test, is well established and associated with only uncommon adverse reactions. Over the last decade, novel skin-based tests for TB infection using TB specific antigens (TBST) have been developed. Evidence on

sections.title: Page 921

summary.text: Summarises key findings: injection site reactions with C-Tb were no more common than with TST and were mostly mild or moderate, while one Chinese report found more reactions with C-TST. Diaskintest safety data were too inconsistent to pool, and overall no safety signal was seen that would affect the choice between the novel tests and TST. The background notes that about a quarter of the world's population has tuberculosis infection.
